title: Messier 78: a reflection nebula in Orion
caption: The reflection nebula Messier 78, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: M 78, Messier 78 · constellation Orion · about 1400 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #17 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This colour portrait shows Messier 78, a reflection nebula in the constellation Orion. The camera behind it is the Wide Field Imager, mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla in Chile.

A reflection nebula is a cloud of dust and gas that we see mainly because it scatters the light of nearby stars, rather than glowing on its own the way energised gas does. The effect is a little like fog lit up by a car's headlights. The cloud itself is dark, but starlight bouncing off its dust makes it visible.

Like most astronomical colour pictures, this one did not come from a single colour snapshot. It was built from many black-and-white exposures, each taken through a different filter (blue, yellow-green, red, and one that isolates light from glowing hydrogen gas). Combining them recreates colour while also highlighting regions where hydrogen shines. The official caption gives little further detail about the nebula itself.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (34.43 x 33.36 arcminutes) and distance (1400 light years), the frame spans roughly 14 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 1,400 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light colour composite was made with the Wide Field Imager, using blue, yellow-green and red filters plus a hydrogen filter. The source does not publish exactly which colour was assigned to each filter in the final picture.
understand.eye: Exposures lasting many minutes collect far more light than the eye, so this faint reflected glow looks much brighter here than it would through a telescope eyepiece.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The total exposure time for each filter was 9 minutes in blue, 9 minutes in yellow-green, 17.5 minutes in red and 15.5 minutes for the hydrogen filter.
alt: The reflection nebula Messier 78, a cloud of dust lit by nearby stars.
